instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Slice the zucchini lengthwise into slices about 1/8 inch thick. Lay them on the baking sheets and sprinkle with 3/4 tsp of the salt. Leave them for 10 minutes.
Press the zucchini dry with paper towels and wipe off the extra salt.
Bake the zucchini for 8 to 10 minutes, until it has softened a little. Pat it dry again and leave the oven on.
Meanwhile, stir the ricotta well and spoon off any liquid on top. Grate the garlic and chop 5 tbsp of the basil.
In a medium bowl, mix the ricotta, 1/4 cup of the Parmesan, the garlic, the egg, 3 tbsp of the basil, the pepper and a pinch of salt.

Spread 1/2 cup of the tomato sauce over the bottom of an 11 x 7 inch baking dish. Lay down a layer of zucchini, then spread on half the ricotta mixture. Sprinkle over a third of the mozzarella and 2 tbsp Parmesan.
Spoon on another 1/2 cup of sauce. Add a second layer of zucchini, the rest of the ricotta mixture, a third of the mozzarella and 2 tbsp Parmesan.
Top with the last of the zucchini, the remaining sauce, the rest of the mozzarella and the last 4 tbsp of Parmesan.
Bake uncovered for 40 to 45 minutes, until it's bubbling at the edges. Turn the oven to broil on high and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the top is browned.
Let it stand for 10 minutes. Sprinkle with the remaining 2 tbsp basil and cut into 4 large squares.
method_notes: A Simple Palate is the lead (salted and pre-baked zucchini slices, a ricotta, egg and basil layer, marinara, mozzarella, a broil at the end). Williams-Sonoma's version also pre-bakes the zucchini but has only 8 ratings. The pre-bake and the salting keep the dish from turning watery. The source makes a 13 x 9 pan; this is about two thirds of it in a smaller dish. It is gluten-free as written, but it honestly takes well over an hour.
